name: credit-rag
tagline: Pulls key terms from credit agreements, each with page and quote

children.title: Document intake
children.summary: Credit agreements come in as PDF uploads or SEC EDGAR HTML. A generator makes a sample agreement with known answers.

children.title: POST /ingest
children.summary: Upload a PDF and get a 202 with a document id right away. Processing carries on in the background.
children.detail: Checks PDF magic bytes and the 25 MB limit. The document id comes from the file's SHA-256, so re-uploading the same file returns already_accepted instead of a duplicate.

children.title: Body-size guard
children.summary: An ASGI middleware enforces the upload cap before the multipart body is buffered, returning 413.
children.detail: Found in review: a size check inside the endpoint runs after parsing and limits nothing. This one covers declared and chunked bodies.

children.title: EDGAR fetch script
children.summary: Pulls a real credit agreement from SEC EDGAR with a pinned URL and SHA-256, so the test document is reproducible.
children.detail: The filing itself stays out of git. Parsed as native HTML because printing to PDF first corrupted text ('Borrower' became 'Bor ower').

children.title: Synthetic agreement
children.summary: Generates a multi-page sample agreement with a pricing-grid table and exact ground truth for regression tests.

children.title: Kafka queue + worker
children.summary: Uploads become events on a Kafka topic. A separate worker processes them, and retries are safe because work is idempotent.

children.title: Versioned events
children.summary: Event contracts are versioned and keyed by document id, so all events for one document stay in order.

children.title: Kafka producer
children.summary: The API publishes an ingest event when Kafka is on. With it off, the same pipeline runs as an in-process background task.
children.detail: Redpanda locally (Kafka API, no ZooKeeper or JVM). Real Kafka is a compose-only swap.

children.title: Idempotent worker
children.summary: At-least-once: offsets commit only after processing. A document already ready is skipped on redelivery.
children.detail: Auto-commit is off. Chunks are replaced with delete+insert, so reprocessing never doubles the index. Emits completed/failed events.

children.title: Atomic claim
children.summary: A single SQL claim makes sure only one worker processes a document. Stuck 'processing' rows are reclaimed after 15 minutes.
children.detail: Closed a duplicate-upload race found in code review.

children.title: CPU work off the event loop
children.summary: Parsing and embedding run in threads so the Kafka consumer keeps sending heartbeats during long documents.
children.detail: Found in a containerized end-to-end run: inline parsing blocked the loop, the consumer got kicked from its group, and redeliveries piled up. asyncio.to_thread fixed it.

children.title: Parse, chunk, embed
children.summary: Each agreement is parsed locally with Docling, split so tables stay whole, embedded locally and stored in pgvector.

children.title: Docling parsing
children.summary: Docling reads PDF and HTML with table-structure recognition on and OCR off, keeping page and heading provenance.
children.detail: Picked over unstructured for stronger open-source table handling. Runs fully local, so document text never leaves the machine at this stage.

children.title: Table-preserving chunker
children.summary: Prose is split by section into 1,200-char pieces with overlap. Tables stay whole as Markdown chunks.
children.detail: Overlap never crosses a table boundary. Each piece is tagged with the page it starts on, so citations stay accurate across page breaks. That's why a rate defined in a pricing grid can still be cited.

children.title: Fail on zero chunks
children.summary: A document that yields no chunks (like a scanned PDF with OCR off) is marked failed, not ready.
children.detail: Cancellations and shutdowns also mark the doc failed with a shielded write, so nothing gets stranded mid-processing.

children.title: Local embeddings
children.summary: bge-small-en-v1.5 embeds chunks locally into 384-d normalized vectors, batched and lazy-loaded.

children.title: pgvector store
children.summary: One Postgres holds documents, chunks and vectors, with an HNSW cosine index and a full-text GIN index.
children.detail: Raw asyncpg and explicit SQL keep the index DDL and the <=> cosine query visible instead of hidden behind an ORM. A generated tsvector column keeps the keyword index in sync.

children.title: Two-pass retrieval
children.summary: Per field group: fast vector + keyword search for recall, then a local cross-encoder re-ranks for precision.

children.title: One query per field group
children.summary: Five focused questions (parties, facility, pricing, covenants, defaults) drive retrieval instead of one big query.

children.title: Vector search
children.summary: Embeds the query and pulls the top 20 nearest chunks from this document via HNSW.

children.title: Keyword search + RRF
children.summary: Postgres full-text search runs alongside and the two ranked lists merge with Reciprocal Rank Fusion (k=60).
children.detail: Rank-based fusion because keyword scores and cosine distance aren't on comparable scales. Measured: it alone didn't move accuracy, but it's kept for literal figures and defined terms.

children.title: Cross-encoder re-rank
children.summary: A local MiniLM cross-encoder scores each query + chunk pair together and keeps the best 5.
children.detail: Stage 1 is cheap recall, stage 2 is precise. Both scores are kept on each result. One env var upgrades to bge-reranker-base.

children.title: Pinned title page
children.summary: The first 2 chunks are always pinned into results, because the borrower's name lives on the title page.
children.detail: 'Borrower' shows up in 288 of 437 chunks, so no ranking can find the one that names it. Adding the title page as a candidate failed too: the re-ranker dropped it. Pinning is what worked.

children.title: Cited extraction
children.summary: Claude fills a strict schema of credit terms from the retrieved chunks, with a page and quote behind every value.

children.title: Credit terms schema
children.summary: Borrower, agent, facility type, amount, maturity, margin, benchmark, events of default, plus a covenants list.
children.detail: Each field carries value, found, citations (chunk id, page, section, verbatim quote) and a rationale. found=false is a valid answer, not an error.

children.title: Attribute groups
children.summary: Fields are extracted in five groups, each with its own retrieval query and sub-schema.

children.title: Versioned prompts
children.summary: System and user prompts live as files: ground in context, cite spans, abstain instead of guessing.
children.detail: Changing a prompt is treated as a measurable event: re-run the eval and compare.

children.title: Instructor + Claude
children.summary: Claude Sonnet 4.6 returns typed output via Instructor, which re-prompts on validation errors (2 retries).

children.title: No-context short-circuit
children.summary: If retrieval returns nothing, the group abstains without spending an LLM call.

children.title: Citation check in code
children.summary: Any value whose citations don't point to a chunk actually retrieved is demoted to NOT FOUND. The model never self-certifies.
children.detail: Covenants with unverifiable citations are dropped. Tested with a mocked LLM that invents a 'ghost' citation.

children.title: Redis result cache
children.summary: Optional cache of extraction results, keyed by content-hash doc id plus model and schema version.
children.detail: Same id always means same content, so a hit can't be stale; including model and schema version means a deploy misses instead of serving old output. Off by default.

children.title: Eval harness
children.summary: Scores retrieval and extraction against hand-labeled answer keys, so every change is proven with numbers.

children.title: Four metrics
children.summary: Context precision, context recall, faithfulness (cited quote is in the cited chunk) and per-field accuracy.
children.detail: Deterministic, no LLM judge needed. Correct abstention counts as correct.

children.title: Golden answer keys
children.summary: A synthetic agreement with exact truth and a hand-labeled 229-page SEC credit agreement.
children.detail: Relevance labels use content markers, so they survive re-chunking.

children.title: Measured A/B
children.summary: Dense only: 57%. Plus keyword search: still 57%. Plus pinned title page: 71%, with the borrower now right.
children.detail: Faithfulness held at 0.875 across all arms and the synthetic set stayed at 1.0. The textbook fix was tested and falsified, then the real cause was found in the data.

children.title: make eval runner
children.summary: Runs the full real pipeline end to end. --mock swaps in a groundable fake extractor, otherwise it calls live Claude.
children.detail: Every retrieval add-on is env-flagged, so any arm can be reproduced.

children.title: API + Angular UI
children.summary: A small FastAPI surface and a single-page Angular app: upload, watch status, then see every term with its citations.

children.title: API routes
children.summary: POST /ingest, GET /documents/{id} for status, POST /extract for results, GET /health, and OpenAPI docs.
children.detail: /extract returns 404, 409 (not ready) or a clear 503 if no model key is set, instead of a fake answer.

children.title: API key auth
children.summary: Every endpoint needs an x-api-key header, compared in constant time. An empty key fails at startup.

children.title: Safe error envelope
children.summary: Errors come back in one client-safe shape with no tracebacks leaked.

children.title: Angular demo UI
children.summary: Angular 19 with signals: drag-drop upload, a status pill polling every 2s, then one card per term.
children.detail: Each card shows the value with page-cited quotes, or a NOT FOUND badge with the reason. Covenants render as a table. Plain CSS, no UI framework.

children.title: Playwright end-to-end
children.summary: Drives the real UI against the live stack and checks every card is either cited or explicitly abstained.
children.detail: The test also captures the README screenshots, so they can't drift from the real UI. Passed with 8/8 attributes and 12 citations.

children.title: Infra + security
children.summary: One Docker image for API and worker, a Compose stack with Kafka and Redis, k8s manifests, and optional Vault secrets.

children.title: One image, two roles
children.summary: Multi-stage uv build, non-root, lockfile-exact deps. The worker is the same image with a different command.
children.detail: No API-vs-worker drift: one build, one set of pinned deps.

children.title: Compose stack
children.summary: API, worker, Postgres+pgvector, Redis and Redpanda, with Vault and the UI behind opt-in profiles.
children.detail: Shared volumes for raw files and the model cache. A containerized run went ingest -> Kafka -> worker -> ready in about 15-18s for the sample doc.

children.title: Kubernetes manifests
children.summary: API Deployment with an autoscaler (2-6 replicas), a worker Deployment, and config/secret maps.
children.detail: Pods run as non-root. Worker replicas share Kafka partitions, so they scale up to the partition count.

children.title: Vault secrets (opt-in)
children.summary: Env vars by default. Set a Vault address and secrets load from Vault KV v2 at startup.

children.title: Locked, reproducible builds
children.summary: uv with a committed lockfile and pinned Python 3.12, after 'green locally, red in CI' drift.
children.detail: Root cause was no lockfile, Python version drift, and an unanchored .gitignore rule that silently left the models package out of the repo.

children.title: Structured logs
children.summary: Standard logging with a JSON formatter switched on for production.

children.title: Tests + CI
children.summary: A fast suite with test doubles runs in about a second, plus marked integration tests against real models, Kafka and pgvector.

children.title: Fast unit suite
children.summary: The LLM and database are swapped for fakes, so tests are quick and give the same result every time.

children.title: Integration tests
children.summary: Marked tests hit real Docling, real models, a real pgvector and a real Redpanda round trip.

children.title: GitHub Actions
children.summary: Two jobs: lint + strict type check + fast tests, and store integration tests against a pgvector service.

children.title: Pre-commit hooks
children.summary: ruff check, ruff format and mypy run before every commit.

children.title: Recorded code reviews
children.summary: Review rounds are written up with findings and fixes, including an adversarial second pass.
children.detail: Round 1: 18 findings confirmed, 23 refuted. Round 2: 7 confirmed, all fixed and re-checked in the containerized stack.

children.title: Planned next
children.summary: Work the repo docs name as next or deferred, each to be proven by the eval harness first.

children.title: Defined-term index
children.summary: Resolve defined terms like 'Revolving Committed Amount' before retrieval, to fix the still-missed facility amount.

children.title: Contextual retrieval + LLM judge
children.summary: Flagged add-ons to A/B against the harness: contextual retrieval and an optional LLM-judge faithfulness signal.

children.title: Alembic migrations
children.summary: Deferred until the schema changes after v1. Plain init SQL is enough for now.

children.title: OpenTelemetry tracing
children.summary: Deferred until there's a collector to send traces to. Logs are already structured JSON.
